learning_outcomes.text: Understand the principles of technical representation and the main projection methods used in industrial drawing.
Know the UNI/CEN/ISO standards governing product technical documentation.
Understand the fundamental principles of 3D CAD modeling and the generation of technical documentation from digital models.
Correctly represent mechanical components through technical sketches and drawings.
Apply the rules for the representation of tolerances and surface roughness specifications.
Create 3D CAD part models and produce the corresponding technical drawings.
Critically analyze technical drawings to extract geometric, functional, and manufacturing information.
Evaluate the correctness and completeness of a technical representation with respect to standards and component functionality.
Select appropriate methods for representation, sectioning, dimensioning, and documentation according to the product being described.
Communicate technical information through drawings, sketches, CAD models, and technical documentation compliant with industrial drawing conventions.
Correctly use the graphical language and technical terminology of mechanical drawing.
Present and justify representation choices adopted for mechanical components and assemblies.
Independently use standards, learning materials, examples, and practical exercises to improve the quality of technical representation.
Progressively develop autonomy in the use of 2D/3D CAD tools and in the preparation of technical documentation.
Transfer the acquired knowledge and skills to subsequent courses and design activities within the Mechanical Engineering curriculum.

syllabus_topics: Modeling, Model Modification, and Feature Management
Drafting and Technical Documentation from CAD

assessment_methods.method: Part I – Technical Drawing and Representation (Multiple-choice theoretical test, Open-ended theoretical questions, Practical freehand drawing test)
Part II – 3D CAD (Practical test using Autodesk Inventor)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 67% from Part I and 33% from Part II, plus an assignment bonus/malus. Assignments 1, 2, and 3 affect the final grade from -1.4 to +1.4 points, with a 0.3-point bonus per assignment for submission within intermediate deadlines. Assignment 4 is a prerequisite for Part II and must be assessed as satisfactory, or admission will be denied. Optional Assignment 5 can award a bonus from 0 to +1.2 points. The two parts of the examination belong to a single session and must be taken within the same session.
